title: [Open Source] Use NVIDIA Kimodo text-to-motion in Blender
author: ppierzc
selftext:
Hey everyone,

A while back I posted about a tool I was building to help generate motion on any character. Got a lot of useful feedback, thanks for that! Today I'm open sourcing two things together: a Blender plugin and a server for running you'd run if you want to run NVIDIA's Kimodo on your own GPU*.*

In the plugin you can set keyframes and add constraints. Output is normal Blender keyframe data on the armature, so all Blender editing and exporting features remain available.

I'm giving you two ways to run it:

* **Self-hosted (locally)** on your own GPU
* **Hosted** on Animatica Cloud (no GPU or setup required)

Everything is open source, the model fork, the backbone, the Blender plugin, and the HTTP protocol (so a Maya/Unreal/Houdini client could be written against the same backend).

Full writeup with install instructions: [https://animatica.ai/kimodo](https://animatica.ai/kimodo)

First public release, would love feedback!

comments.author: Deep_State_Probe
comments.body: Do you need a specific rig for this and how much GPU VRAM is needed?

replies.author: ppierzc
replies.body: You need 17GB VRAM to run the full model on GPU, there are options to run it with 3GB with parts offloaded to the CPU, though that makes it slower. (There is also the cloud option with free generation credits to check out the plugin without needing local setup first) Self hosted currently only supports the SOMA skeleton, cloud uses our ML retargeter which works quite well with most humanoid characters in T-pose.
